paper.abstract_en: The Institute for Nuclear Physics at the University of Mainz operates the electron accelerator MAMI. It provides a polarized electron beam with an intensity of up to 100 𝜇A and a polarization degree of about 80%. In the near future, the superconducting energy-recovering electron accelerator MESA will be commissioned. It will deliver significantly higher beam intensities, thereby enabling a new generation of high-precision experiments. In the energy- recovery mode, for internal targets beam intensities of up to 1 mA at a beam energy of 105 MeV are planned, while for external targets operated without energy recovery, intensities of up to 150 𝜇A at 155 MeV are expected. The degree of polarization is anticipated to reach 85%. This articlereports on polarized-electron beam experiments carried out at the existing accelerator and on planned experiments at the new facility currently under construction, with a particular emphasis on the P2 experiment at MESA.
